A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UAE/Unified-GRPO research, despite the changed title and substantial revision. The main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original UAE generation, caption-quality, and reconstruction results in Tables 1–6, alongside qualitative experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original UAE results and adds post-training comparisons on two architectures, MMT-Bench evaluations, and a visual-encoder freezing ablation.

M1.justification: v1 specifies joint cold-start training, caption-policy RL, and diffusion-policy RL, including an alternative image-embedding condition. v4 instead specifies LLM-only reconstruction RL with frozen visual modules for hybrid models and introduces a shared autoregressive implementation for understanding and generation (Section 2.2; supplementary Section 3). These change the proposed training procedure and architectural scope.

E1.justification: v4 adds MMBench and MMMU evaluations in Table 1 and extensive MMT-Bench coverage in Tables 7–8, including localization, object recognition, person re-identification, OCR, and document understanding. This substantially extends v1's generation, captioning, and reconstruction evaluation. GenEval, GenEval++, DPG-Bench, and Unified-Bench remain covered.

E2.justification: The GenEval table removes dedicated generation methods and several older unified baselines while adding X-Omni. GenEval++ removes its dedicated-generation rows. DPG-Bench adds Playground v2.5 and PixArt-Σ while retaining earlier comparators. New MMT-Bench comparisons include InternVL-Chat-v1.2-34B, GPT-4V, LLaVA-v1.5-7B, and guessing controls.

E3.justification: v4 adds paired baseline/post-training comparisons for UniWorld and Janus-Pro across understanding, generation, and reconstruction metrics. It also introduces accuracy evaluations at MMT-Bench meta-task and selected fine-grained-subtask levels, with a stated averaging rule. These are new evaluation designs; the retained 100-image reconstruction and four-judge caption comparisons preserve their basic designs.

E4.justification: v4 adds the two-architecture post-training ablation (Table 1), frozen versus unfrozen visual-encoder comparison (Figure 9), long-prompt generation comparisons, and visual-difference/grounding case studies (Figures 4 and 7). v1's informal analysis of long-caption versus image-embedding conditioning is omitted. The training curves are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4's disclosure of four GRPO samples per prompt concerns training-time sampling, not independent experimental repetitions or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results in Tables 1, 7, and 8, including fine-grained MMT-Bench accuracy of 32.5 versus 56.9 and OCR accuracy of 75.0 versus 68.8 for its baseline and trained model. Existing UAE headline values remain 86.09 on Unified-Bench, 0.86/0.89 on GenEval, 0.475 on GenEval++, and 84.74 on DPG-Bench. The new comparisons do not establish version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, advantage normalization, and cosine reconstruction reward remain mathematically equivalent. v4 removes the separate cold-start loss and diffusion-trajectory likelihood-ratio formulations in v1 Equations 3–4 as those stages disappear. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The auto-encoder principle remains central, but v1 foregrounds a bespoke three-stage framework, a first unification benchmark, and an emergent 'aha moment.' v4 foregrounds broadly applicable post-training across architectural families and direct fine-grained perception benefits, while qualifying understanding improvements through OCR-related tradeoffs. This substantially changes the contribution framing and claim scope.

C2.justification: v4 connects observed OCR/document-understanding declines to imperfect text generation and potentially misleading reconstruction rewards, and explains limited general understanding gains through generator weaknesses. It adds a stability rationale for freezing the visual encoder. v1's discussions of conditioning equivalence, editing, and connector evolution are removed, while possible audio/video extensions are introduced.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies learning rate, batch size, GRPO group size, KL coefficient, sampling temperature and prompt, Unified-Bench's LAION-5B source, and full generation-example prompts. It no longer documents v1's 700K/50K pretraining recipe and LoRA setup. The repository link is omitted and replaced by a promise to release resources upon publication; actual external availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds a substantial related-work survey covering unified architectures, generative RL, and evaluation, including discussions of MAR, Harmon, DanceGRPO, and UniEval. It explicitly relates its autoregressive implementation to T2I-R1 and AR-GRPO. Several earlier citations, including Cycle Consistency as Reward, disappear, and positioning shifts toward post-training existing unified models.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and methodology are substantially rewritten. The standalone benchmark section becomes part of methodology, experiments are reorganized around architectural ablations and understanding evaluations, and the extended discussion is replaced by a shorter limitations/conclusion section. A structured seven-section supplement replaces the earlier supplementary figure pages.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the overview and architecture diagrams, adds ablation and understanding tables, and introduces several comparison figures. DPG-Bench and existing qualitative material move to the supplement; training curves become a standalone figure. The generation montage gains sample labels, and the GenEval++ qualitative grid is shortened.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens evidence beyond v1's caption/reconstruction-based understanding tests through architectural controls and direct understanding evaluations. Explicit OCR/document-understanding limitations and RL settings improve interpretation and reproducibility. However, introduced reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 8 says Overall averages the displayed subtasks, yet InternVL's reported 63.4 differs from their mean of 54.88. The added evidence is useful, but its comparative summaries require reconciliation.
